The statute described outlines the core requirements for valid consent under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Legally, this means that consent cannot be assumed through silence, pre-ticked boxes, or inactivity. Instead, it must be an affirmative action that is freely given (without coercion), specific (for distinct processing activities), informed (the individual knows what they are agreeing to), and unambiguous (clearly indicating agreement). For businesses, this imposes a strict obligation to implement transparent data collection practices and maintain records of consent. For individuals, it reinforces their right to privacy and control over their personal information, ensuring that data processing only occurs when there is a clear, active agreement.
